review_notes: I read the whole file. I grepped Mathlib for uses of Equiv.traversable, Equiv.isLawfulTraversable, Equiv.functor and Equiv.lawfulFunctor. The only live consumer is Mathlib/Data/DList/Instances.lean (lines 38 and 41), which passes DList.listEquivDList directly to Equiv.traversable and Equiv.isLawfulTraversable. The only other hit is a commented-out sketch in Mathlib/Logic/Equiv/Array.lean. The family of equivalences is passed around as a plain `∀ α, t α ≃ t' α`. A bundled structure, for example a natural equivalence of type functors, would not simplify either use, and a single consumer gives no evidence it would help. I did not check whether Mathlib has a natural-isomorphism interface suited to this setting. Separate Equiv.map/Equiv.traverse definitions and the primed lemma variants exist for non-canonical instances, so they are not missing structure. I report no finding.
